subject: BioGeoBEARS validation tests, including Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM)

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: BioGeoBEARS validation tests, including Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM)
parts:
Hi all,

Short version: I have posted a bunch of validation examples to: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation, and gotten stochastic mapping to be consistent with ancestral state probabilities. Everyone should source the new validated code, whether or not they are doing stochastic mapping at the moment. The source() commands are near the top of the example script: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script


Long version: It took some serious digging in the code, but I have finally figured out what the issue was with the preliminary stochastic mapping code that I created last year. My expectation was that if one did many stochastic maps under the ML model and took the average, this should equal the ancestral state probabilities calculated analytically under the ML model.  The problem was that this was only roughly true in my earlier tests -- state probabilities, especially those with the highest-uncertainty (probabilities between 0.25 and 0.75) tended to correlate with the analytic probabilities less than expected. 

There were several subtle issues I had to fix including a default fixed value for a random number seed (I was changing the seed progressively in an early experiment, but it was too easy to forget), details of using the uppass calculation, and try statements to catch errors when the simulation step is attempting to simulate a valid history on a branch.

As part of figuring this out I set up a number of validation examples to test ancestral state probabilities between normal and stratified BioGeoBEARS, between them and Liam Revell's phytools (for a case where BioGeoBEARS can implement the phytools unordered character model). I haven't tried comparison to diversitree stochastic mapping but I did show the ClaSSE model can be reduced to equal the various BioGeoBEARS models.

The validation is posted here:

Biogeobears Validation
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation

Basically, everything now lines up well compared in several different ways, and this is good evidence that both the ancestral state probabilities and the BSM are working correctly, in both the non-stratified and stratified versions.

I won't claim it's perfect (post issues to the Google Group as always), but I'm happy enough with it to add the updates to the source() commands at the beginning of the script. As usual, after every library(BioGeoBEARS) command, source the revised code:

================

Yes, this source() thing is getting ridiculous, but it's only until I get a new CRAN version up. An alternative that takes up less space in your script is to download all of these files to some directory and use the BioGeoBEARS sourceall() command to source all of the .R files in that directory.

The best example code for stochastic mapping at the moment is "Psychotria_M0_unconstrained_BSMs.zip", at: 
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation#BGB_nonstrat_DEC_DECj

You will have to make your own modifications to source the code above, set your working directory, etc. I eventually hope to have a tutorial etc. that runs automatically on defaults, but that will take awhile.

Cheers,
Nick
